summary: All visitors to Kenya, including infants and children, need an approved Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) from etakenya.go.ke before the journey (from USD 30), unless exempt: citizens of the East African Community partner states (up to 180 days) and of the countries listed in the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025 for 90 or 60 days, among them most African countries, including South Africa, many Caribbean and Pacific island states, and Singapore, Malaysia and Cyprus. Every traveller must also hold Inbound Travel Health Insurance issued under Kenya's Insurance Regulatory Authority (Ministry of Health, Gazette Notice No. 11492 of 30 July 2026).

fee.notes: From USD 30 for normal processing (up to 72 hours); expedited, immediate processing costs USD 100 more. The standard eTA allows one entry; the portal also lists a one-year multiple-entry eTA (USD 300), a five-year multiple-entry eTA for US citizens (USD 185) and a transit eTA (USD 20). Travellers who are not exempt need one, including infants and children.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. WHO recommends vaccination for all travellers aged 9 months or over, except those whose itineraries are limited to the North Eastern Province; Kilifi, Kwale, Lamu, Malindi and Tana River in the Coast Province; and the cities of Nairobi and Mombasa.

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health: country list of vaccination requirements (2022, revised 2023)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: The US CDC says malaria is transmitted in all areas of Kenya below 2,500 m, including game parks, with rare cases in the highly urbanized centre of Nairobi, and recommends prescription medicine to prevent malaria for travellers to those areas; for central Nairobi it recommends insect bite precautions only.

travelInsurance.text: Kenya's Ministry of Health requires all travellers to Kenya to hold valid Inbound Travel Health Insurance issued under the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA), under Gazette Notice No. 11492 (Vol. CXXVIII, No. 129, 30 July 2026). The eTA application shows this notice before payment and lets you check your insurance status or obtain the cover. No minimum cover or price is stated there.

notes: The Government of Canada says the use, manufacture or importation of plastic bags, including garbage and shopping bags, is illegal in Kenya; offenders, including tourists, can face fines of up to USD 40,000, up to two years in prison, or both.

The Kenya Revenue Authority's duty-free allowance: spirits (including liqueurs) or wine up to 1 liter, or wine up to 2 liters; perfume and toilet water up to half a liter, of which no more than a quarter may be perfume; and cigarettes, cigars, cheroots, cigarillos, tobacco and snuff up to 250 g in all.

safety.text: Because of the risk of terrorism from groups based in Somalia, the UK Foreign Office (FCDO) advises against all travel to Mandera County, parts of Wajir County, most of Garissa County and Lamu County except Lamu Island and Manda Island, and against all but essential travel to Garissa Town, Tana River County north of the Tana River as far as Saka, and the coast within 15 km between the Tana and Galana rivers.

tips.text: Apply for the Kenya eTA only at the official portal etakenya.go.ke, where the fee starts at USD 30.
The Government of Canada warns that plastic bags are illegal in Kenya — using or importing them can bring fines of up to USD 40,000, up to two years in prison, or both.
According to the Government of Canada, national parks do not accept cash: they generally take credit cards, but at times, because of technical problems, only M-PESA mobile money works.
The Government of Canada describes M-PESA mobile money as a common form of payment accepted across Kenya, including at national parks.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Kenya?
faq.answer: US citizens need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA), applied for at etakenya.go.ke before the journey. The standard eTA costs USD 30 and allows one entry; the portal says processing typically takes three working days, and it does not state the length of stay. US citizens can also apply for a five-year multiple-entry eTA (USD 185).

faq.question: Is the Kenya eTA the same as a visa?
faq.answer: The eTA portal says the eTA replaces traditional visa requirements for most travellers. It is a permission to travel, applied for online at etakenya.go.ke before entering Kenya and costing from USD 30, and holding one is not the final authority to enter: admissibility is decided at the point of entry. Citizens of the East African Community partner states and of the countries listed in the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025, including most African countries, Singapore, Malaysia and Cyprus, are exempt.

faq.question: How early should I apply for the Kenya eTA?
faq.answer: The eTA portal says applications are usually processed in 3 days, with an urgent processing service available, and recommends applying at least 2 weeks before travel. The approved eTA must be shown at all departure and arrival points.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Kenya?
faq.answer: It is required only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. WHO recommends vaccination for travellers aged 9 months or over, except those staying only in certain areas, including the cities of Nairobi and Mombasa. The Government of Canada adds that Kenyan authorities regularly carry out spot checks for proof of yellow fever vaccination, and advises carrying a copy at all times.

faq.question: When is the best time for a Kenya safari?
faq.answer: No official source gives a best safari season. The Government of Canada says Kenya's two rainy seasons usually run from October to November and from March to mid-June, varying from year to year, and that seasonal flooding can hamper overland travel. It also says national parks do not accept cash.
